name: co.humanome/humanome
title: Humanome
description: Anatomy picture quizzes on a 3D body, real histology slides and lab practical lists for students.

tools.name: quiz_anatomy_structures
tools.description: Quiz a student on human anatomy with pictures: each question shows one structure lit up on a 3D human body (a bone, muscle, nerve, vessel, brain part or organ) with four names to choose from. Give a topic in the student's words (a region, a system or a lab practical, such as 'upper limb muscles', 'cranial nerves', 'bones of the skull' or 'muscles lab practical'), or the names on the student's own lab list. Use it when a student asks to be quizzed or tested on anatomy or to practise for an anatomy lab practical. Not for physiology calculations, diseases or medical advice.

topic.description: What to be quizzed on, in the student's words: a region, a body system, a structure group or a lab practical.

structures.description: A course's own list of structure names to be quizzed on, used instead of a topic.

tools.name: quiz_histology_slides
tools.description: Quiz a student on identifying tissues on real microscope slides (epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous tissue): each question shows a slide with its magnification and four tissue names, the wrong ones being tissues that look alike. Use it when a student wants to practise tissue identification or a histology practical.

tissue_type.description: Which kind of tissue, or all.

tools.name: look_up_anatomy_structure
tools.description: Look up one structure of the human body by name (spellings and abbreviations from a lab sheet work too): what it is in one or two sentences, its body system, a picture of it lit on a 3D body, its reference page and the quizzes that ask it. Use it when a student asks what or where a structure is.

name.description: The structure's name, e.g. 'deltoid', 'foramen magnum', 'm. sartorius'.

tools.name: list_lab_practical_structures
tools.description: List the structures an anatomy and physiology lab practical asks, section by section (for example the bones, the muscles, the brain, the heart, blood vessels, the nervous system, A&P 1 or A&P 2), with links to practise each. Use it when a student asks what to study for a lab practical or wants a checklist of structures.

practical.description: The practical or course unit, e.g. 'muscles', 'appendicular skeleton', 'A&P 2'.
